comments.en: The early commentaries ask how this can be reconciled with the Gemara (Gittin 4b) that states that witnesses are available to ratify a bill of divorce throughout Eretz Yisrael, which indicates that there is free travel throughout Eretz Yisrael, including between Judea and the Galilee. They answer that with regard to a bill of divorce, the wife actively seeks out witnesses and will be able to find a few individuals who have traveled from one province to the other. With regard to a protest, the matter depends on the word spreading naturally. This will happen only if there is free travel between the localities (Tosafot; Rashba).

comments.en:
דסתם יהודה וגליל כשעת חירום דמי—For generally יהודה and גליל are like in a state of emergency

OVERVIEW
The משנה stated that there is no חזקה between יהודה and גליל, even though generally מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה, because יהודה וגליל are considered to be כשעת חירום and there is no free flow of information from one to the other. תוספות contrasts this ruling regarding חזקה with a different ruling regarding the בפני נכתב ונחתם of a גט.
--------------------------
תוספות asks:
ואם תאמר ומאי שנא דגבי גט אמר בריש גיטין (דף ד,ב ושם דיבור המתחיל כיון) –
And if you will say; and why is there this difference that regarding גט where the משנה states in the beginning of מסכת גיטין –
המביא גט ממדינה למדינה בארץ ישראל אין צריך לומר בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם –
A שליח who brings a גט from one country to another country in א"י is not required to say בפ"נ ובפ"נ; the גמרא there explains, the reason is –
משום כיון דאיכא עולי רגלים משכח שכיחי לקיימו –
Because since there are עולי רגלים, witnesses will definitely be found to authenticate the גט. The גמרא there continues –
ואפילו בזמן שאין בית המקדש כיון דאיכא בתי דינים דקביעי משכח שכיחי –
And even nowadays when the ביהמ"ק is not [existing], nevertheless, since there are established courts of law, עדים will surely be found to be מקיים this גט. The question is why regarding a גט there will be עדים מצויין לקיימו (even from יהודה לגליל), regardless that it is כשעת חירום, however regarding מחאה, our משנה maintains that since יהודה וגליל is כשעת חירום דמי, therefore no one will hear the מחאה. If there are sufficient travelers for קיום there should be sufficient travelers for a מחאה and vice versa.
תוספות answers:
ויש לומר דודאי גבי גט מצויין לקיימו אפילו מיהודה לגליל –
And one can say; that certainly regarding גט it is מצויין לקיימו even from יהודה to גליל; the reason is –
לפי שהאשה רגילה לחזר אחר עדי קיום –
Since it is natural for the woman to search for עדי קיום –
אבל הכא אי לאו דשכיחי טובא לעולם לא ישמע מחאתו –
However here regarding a חזקה and מחאה, if it would not be very common for people to travel מיהודה לגליל, the מחזיק would never hear of this מחאה –
שאין המחזיק רגיל לחזר אם מוחה לו ואם לאו –
Since it is not usual that the מחזיק inquire whether the מ"ק is מוחה or not –
הלכך בשיירות דעולי רגלים ובתי דינין לא סגי –
Therefore the caravans of the עולי רגלים or the בתי דינים are not sufficient that he will hear the מחאה, rather it is necessary that they reside in the same ארץ (מדינה), where there will much more people traveling from place to place to publicize the מחאה.
תוספות asks:
ואם תאמר והא דאמרינן התם (דף ו,א) רב ששת מצריך (מערסא לערסא) –
And if you will say; and regarding this which the גמרא states there in מס' גיטין that ר"ש required saying בפ"נ even when a גט was brought from one [שכונה] to a neighboring [שכונה] –
ורבא מצריך אפילו באותה שכונה –
And רבא required saying בפ"נ even if the גט was brought within the same שכונה –
ופריך והא רבא הוא דאמר לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו ומשני שאני בני מחוזא דניידי –
And the גמרא questioned this ruling of רבא; ‘but רבא is the one who maintains that the reason for saying בפ"נ is because (if a גט is brought from חו"ל to א"י) there will not be עדים available to be מקיים the גט’, however in one שכונה there will certainly be people who recognize the חתימה of people in the same שכונה. And the גמרא there answers; ‘the בני מחוזא are different from other people because they are constantly on the move’. Therefore it is possible that neighbors may not recognize the signature of their neighbors. This concludes the citation of the גמרא in גיטין. Now תוספות concludes his question –
אטו מי נימא דבמחוזא מחאה שלא בפניו לא הוי מחאה ויצטרך לבא לפניו למחות –
Shall we say then that in מחוזא a מחאה שלא בפניו will not be a מחאה (just as we say that there are no עדים מצויין לקיימו in מחוזא [since they are ניידי]), and it will be necessary for the מערער to come in the presence of the מחזיק to make a מחאה?!
תוספות answers:
ויש לומר דלא דמי דכשחותמים על הגט במחוזא והולכין להן –
And one can say; that the two cases (of קיום and מחאה in מחוזא) are not comparable, for when the people of מחוזא sign on a גט and go on their business journey –
אין דרך שיצעקו בעיר אנחנו חתמנו על גט פלוני –
It is not customary that the עדים will shout in the city we signed on his גט –
אבל במחאה דרך הליכתם רגילות לומר פלוני מיחה ושומעין אחרים עד שנשמע בבית המחזיק:
However by מחאה it is customary that on their journey they tell others that so and so made a מחאה and others hear about it and repeat it to their friends until it is heard in the sמחזיק' house.

SUMMARY
Regarding ממדינה למדינה the woman will find the עדי קיום (she is seeking), more readily than the מחזיק will hear the מחאה (which he is not anticipating); however regarding בני מחוזא דניידי, it will be easier to hear the מחאה (through חברא חברא אית ליה) than to find the עדי קיום who are on the go, and not available.

THINKING IT OVER
תוספות writes אין דרך שיצעקו בעיר אנחנו חתמנו, etc. Can we infer from תוספות that if they would announce that they signed, and others heard them, can the others be מקיים the שטר based on what they heard (עד מפי עד)?

en:
מחי, מָחָה, (מָחַח) (Biblical Hebrew; see מָהָה) to rub, wipe out; to wear out, destroy. [In Talmud mostly מָחַק.] Eruvin 13ᵃ; Sotah II, 4 (17ᵇ) (reference. to ומחה, Bamidbar V, 23) כתב שיכול לִמְחוֹת (Mishnah להִמָּחֵק) a writing which one can wash off. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 23 (play on מחויאל, Breishit IV, 18) מוֹחָן אני וכ׳ I shall wipe them out of the world; and e.—V. מָחוּי.

Piël - מִיחָה [to strike out, annul,]
1) to protest against. Bava Batra 38ᵇ מי׳ בפני שנים if he entered a protest against the illegitimate occupation of his property in the presence of two (see מְחָאָה). Ib. וכי למָחוֹת וכ׳ must he protest in the occupant’s presence?—Ketubot 11ᵃ מִיחֲתָה she protested against her conversion in childhood. Pesachim 88ᵃ יכולה למחות she has the privilege of protesting (declaring her preference); and from

—2) (with ב or ביד of the person) to forewarn, interfere, try to prevent. Shabbat 55ᵇ bottom of page מפני שהיה לו … בחפני ולא מי׳ (not לחפני, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) it was for Ph. to forewarn Hofni, and he did not. Ib.ᵃ שאם מִיחוּ בהם לא יקבלו מהם (Manuscript Munich מחו … קבלו) that if they warned them, they would not have heeded them. Pesachim IV, 8, and e. לא מיחו בידם they did not prohibit their doing so; and from—Shir HaShirim Rabbah to IV, 12 עמדו הבנות (ו)מִיחוּ על עצמן וכ׳ the daughters (in their father’s absence) entered a protest concerning themselves and gave themselves away to husbands (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Beshalach, p. 82ᵃ, and e. נתעסקו בעצמן).

Hifil - הִמְחָה
1) to dissolve, dilute. Yerushalmi Pesachim III, beginning 29ᵈ ה׳ את החמץ if (by boiling) he made a mush of the leavened matter (made it unrecognizable). Chullin 120ᵃ; Yerushalmi Ma'aser Sheni II, beginning 53ᵇ, and e., see גָּמָא; and from (interchanging with הִמְהָה).—Tosefta Parah IX (VIII), 8 הִמְחָן באור (not באויר) if he thawed the frozen water by artificial heat.—[Midrash Till. to Psalms VI, 7 וממחה, read וממסה, see מָסָה.]

—2) to rub off, cleanse, polish. Bava Batra V, 10 מַמְחֶה משקלותיו cleanses his weights. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 7 (play on מיחים, Psalms LXVI, 15) כזה שהוא ממחה בקערה like him who wipes a dish (licks the remnants up); Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Eth Korb., p. 61ᵃ; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 16; and e.—Pirké d’R. El. Chaldaic XVII מַמְחָה בכפיה she produces a sound by rubbing her hands (in sympathy with the mourners).

—3) (denominative of מוּמְחֶה) to recognize as an authority; in gen. to authorize; to appoint. Sanhedrin 23ᵃ לא כל הימנו … שהִמְחוּהוּ רבים עליהם he cannot reject a judge whom the majority has recognized as an authority over them. Bava Metzia IX, 12 הִמְחֵהוּ אצל וכ׳ if he gave him an order to the storekeeper. Yerushalmi Pesachim VIII, 35ᵈ top אם במַמְחִין סתם האשה מַמְחָה וכ׳ if by מדעתו is meant giving authority (and not merely knowing and tolerating), it is tacitly understood that a woman makes an appointment as if saying, I will dine with my children; if it means merely knowing, then the Mishnah (Pesachim VIII, 1) means appointment.—[Y. Shabbat XIII, beginning 14ᵃ הממחה צדדיו ed. Krot., see מָתַח.]

Nifal - נִמְחֶה to be dissolved, washed away; to be wiped out, destroyed. Yerushalmi Pesachim III, beginning 29ᵈ a cake boiled שלא נ׳ without being mashed beyond recognition (see supra). Taanit III, 8, and e. אם נִמְחֵית וכ׳, whether the stone … has been washed away, see אֶבֶן. Tosefta Parah l. common gender. נִימּוֹחוּ (from מָחַח) the water was thawed up. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 28. אפי׳ אסטרובולין … נ׳ even the millstone was washed away. Ib. וכמה נימוחו מהם and how many of them were destroyed?; and e.

comments.en:
אין מחזיקין בנכסי בורח—One cannot make a חזקה in the properties of an escapee

OVERVIEW
רב ruled that a חזקה which is made on the property of a בורח is not a valid חזקה, since the בורח cannot come and be מוחה in the presence of the מחזיק (for רב agrees with ר"י that מחאה שלא בפניו לא הוי מחאה). תוספות discusses what is meant by בורח, and how we justify this ruling of רב.
-------------------------
בבורח מחמת ממון איירי דאי מחמת מרדין בהא לא פליג שמואל כדמוכח בסמוך –
We are discussing one who runs away for monetary reasons, however if he is בורח on account of murder, שמואל would not argue with רב in such a case, as is evident shortly in the גמרא.
ודוקא בבורח אבל באיניש דעלמא הויא חזקה שיכול לבא למקום שמחזיק שם ולמחות –
And it is specifically regarding a בורח that you cannot make a חזקה on his properties, however by a regular person who is not living there, it is a valid חזקה, since that person can come to the place where he is making the חזקה and protest –
אבל בורח אינו רשאי לבא במקום שעומד לא הויא מחאה שלא בפניו –
However a בורח who is not able to come to the place where the מחזיק is staying, it is not a מחאה [for it is] שלא בפניו, and therefore the חזקה is no חזקה –
וסבר לה כרבי יהודה דקתני ויבא לשנה אחרת וימחה משמע שצריך למחות בפניו –
For רב agrees with ר"י who states in the משנה, ‘and he (the מערער) will come the next (third) year and protest’; indicating that it is necessary to protest in the presence of the מחזיק.
תוספות questions the previous assumption that ר"י maintains מחאה שלא בפניו לא הויא מחאה:
ואם תאמר ודלמא רבי יהודה נמי לא בעי מחאה בפניו –
And if you will say; but perhaps ר"י does not require a מחאה בפניו –
והכי קאמר ויבא במדינה שהמחזיק בה וימחה –
And this is what ר"י is saying, ‘and the מערער will come to the country where the מחזיק is and be מוחה’ in that country (but not necessarily in the presence of the מחזיק) –
כגון אם הוא ביהודה יבא ביהודה וימחה שאז תשמע מחאתו –
For instance if the מחזיק is in יהודה (and the מערער is in אספמיא), the מערער will come to יהודה and be מוחה, for then his מחאה will be heard even though it is שלא בפניו, because (even ר"י agrees that) מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה.
In summation; תוספות is asking that perhaps ר"י agrees with the רבנן that מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה and when ר"י states ויבא לשנה אחרת, he means that he will come and be מוחה in the מדינה where the מחזיק is but not בפני המחזיק.
תוספות anticipates a difficulty (with his proposal that ר"י agrees to מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה):
וכי תימא וכיון שחזקה נשמעת עד אספמיא גם המחאה תשמע עד אספמיא –
And if you will say [that] since the חזקה is heard as far as אספמיא, we can assume that also the מחאה will be heard as far as אספמיא; תוספות concludes the difficulty –
ואי מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה ליתיב אדוכתיה ולימחי –
And if מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה (as תוספות suggested in his question), let the מערער sit in his place in אספמיא and be מוחה and it will be heard in א"י. The fact that he has to leave אספמיא (seemingly) proves that מחאה שלא בפניו לא הוי מחאה –
In summation; the preceding וכי תימא assumes that a מחאה is heard the same as a חזקה is heard, and therefore we cannot assume that ר"י maintains מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה, for then there is no need for him to leave אספמיא to make a מחאה, when he can make the מחאה in אספמיא and it will be heard in א"י, just as the חזקה in א"י was heard in אספמיא. This would answer תוספות question.
תוספות rejects this assumption (of the וכי תימא) that a מחאה is equally known as a חזקה:
הא ליתא דאי כל מקום שחזקה נשמעת גם המחאה נשמעת –
This assumption (that wherever you can hear the חזקה, you can also hear the מחאה) is not so! For if we were to assume that wherever the חזקה is heard, the מחאה is also heard and there is no difference between the publicity of a חזקה and the publicity of a מחאה –
אם כן היכי מוכח לעיל דלרבנן מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה –
If indeed this is so, how did the גמרא prove earlier that the רבנן of ר"י maintain מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה –
אימא דלעולם דלא הוי מחאה והיה ביהודה והחזיק ביהודה הוי חזקה –
I can say that in truth a מחאה שלא בפניו is not a מחאה, and the reason why if the מערער was in יהודה and the חזקה was in יהודה it is a חזקה (is not because a מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה, but rather) –
לפי שהיא נשמעת ויבא וימחה לפני המחזיק –
Because the חזקה is heard everywhere in יהודה and so the מערער will come and be מוחה in the presence of the מחזיק –
אבל מיהודה לגליל אין החזקה נשמעת ומשום הכי לא הויא חזקה –
However from יהודה to גליל the חזקה is not heard so far away, and therefore it is not a חזקה (but not because מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה). However since we see that the גמרא derives from the ruling of the רבנן that מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה we must –
אלא ודאי פשיטא ליה לגמרא דהחזקה נשמעת מרחוק אבל מחאה לא –
Rather assume that it is certainly obvious to the גמרא that a חזקה can be heard from afar, however not a מחאה; it cannot be heard as far as a חזקה –
ולהכי מוכח לעיל שפיר דסברי רבנן דהויא מחאה שלא בפניו –
And therefore the גמרא previously correctly proved that the רבנן maintain that a מחאה שלא בפניו is valid –
דאי לא הויא מחאה אלא צריך לבא לפני המחזיק –
For if it is not a valid מחאה, but rather the מערער is required to appear before the מחזיק –
אם כן מיהודה לגליל תהא חזקה -–
If indeed it is true, so there should be a חזקה even from יהודה to גליל –
כמו שביהודה יש לו לילך ולמחות מיהודה לגליל נמי ילך לפניו וימחה –
for just as in יהודה the מערער is required to go and be מוחה in the sמחזיק' presence (for we are now assuming מחאה שלא בפניו לא הוי מחאה), so too from יהודה to גליל the מערער should also go and be מוחה in the sמחזיק' presence, but since we see that there is no חזקה מיהודה לגליל, the only explanation is that the מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה, however the מחאה does not travel as far as the חזקה, therefore in יהודה the מחאה שלא בפניו will reach the מחזיק but not from יהודה לגליל.
In summation; we can either assume that חזקה ומחאה are heard equally or that חזקה can be heard more than מחאה. If we assume that a חזקה is heard further than a מחאה (it can be heard מיהודה לגליל), we can understand how רב derives that the רבנן maintain מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה. The חזקה is heard both in יהודה and גליל, the only way to explain why it is a חזקה in יהודה and not in גליל is if we assume that the מחאה is made שלא בפניו, therefore מיהודה ליהודה it will be heard and מיהודה לגליל the מחאה will not be heard (even though the חזקה will be heard מיהודה לגליל). However if we require a מחאה בפניו what is the difference between יהודה and גליל. This is all true if we maintain that the חזקה is more publicized than the מחאה.
However if we assume (as the 'וכי תימא' does) that the publicity of a חזקה ומחאה are equal, then we can easily explain the difference between יהודה and גליל (without assuming מחאה שלא בפניו הוי מחאה); in יהודה it is a חזקה, since the חזקה is heard in יהודה the מחזיק will come and be מוחה בפניו, however in גליל where the חזקה is not heard there can be no מחאה or חזקה; why did רב assume that the רבנן maintain מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה. This proves again that we must assume that a חזקה is heard further than a מחאה and מחאה שלא בפניו is a valid מחאה according to the רבנן. The question remains perhaps ר"י also agrees that מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה, so why does רב rule אין מחזיקין בנכסי בורח, if he can make a מחאה שלא בפניו.
תוספות answers:
ויש לומר מדלא תני רבי יהודה אומר ויבא לשנה אחרת וימחה ויודיעהו –
And one can say; we know that ר"י maintains מחאה שלא בפניו לא הויא מחאה, since the משנה did not state and the מערער will come the following (third) year and protest, and [they] will inform the מחזיק –
שמע מינה שצריך למחות לפניו. רבינו יצחק:
We can derive from this that he must be מוחה in the presence of the מחזיק. This (תוספות) is attributed to the ר"י.

SUMMARY
The ruling of רב is only by בורח (מחמת ממון), but not by a person who left willingly. ר"י maintains that a מחאה must be בפניו, since he did not state ויודיעוהו.

THINKING IT OVER
1. From תוספות here it seems that if we maintain מחאה שלא בפניו לא הוי מחאה, it would be incumbent on the מערער to travel (even from מדינה למדינה and certainly) מעיר לעיר to make a מחאה. However previously תוספות taught that if מחאה שלא בפניו לא הוי מחאה, then it will not be a חזקה, but the מערער will not be required to travel מעיר לעיר!
2. תוספות writes that if we maintain (according to the רבנן) that מחאה שלא בפניו לא הוי מחאה, then just as the מערער is required to travel מיהודה ליהודה and make a מחאה בפניו he should also be required to travel מיהודה לגליל and make the מחאה בפניו. However how can we compare the two cases; perhaps the חכמים only required him to come a short distance (מיהודה ליהודה), but not a far (and dangerous) distance (מיהודה לגליל)?!

sections.en: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says: One cannot establish the presumption of ownership with regard to the property of one who is fleeing, as he is unable to lodge a protest. Rav Yehuda reports: When I said this ruling before Shmuel, he disagreed and said to me: But does the owner actually have to protest in the presence of the possessor? Since that is not the case, and he can lodge a protest wherever he is, one can establish the presumption of ownership with regard to the property of one who is fleeing.

sections.en: The Gemara asks: And Rav, who ruled that one cannot establish the presumption of ownership with regard to the property of one who is fleeing, what is he teaching us, that a protest that is lodged not in his presence is not a valid protest? But doesn’t Rav say: A protest that is lodged not in his presence is a valid protest? The Gemara answers: Rav was explaining the reason of the tanna of our mishna, but he himself does not hold accordingly. Rav holds, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, that the protest is valid.

comments.en: Since the owner is fleeing, he is unable to protest. While the same halakha would apply whenever the owner is in a situation preventing him from lodging a protest, the Gemara chose this particular example because it is the most likely scenario in which someone would seize his property unlawfully, as he would not be concerned that the owner will return (Rashbam). The Jerusalem Talmud offers proof for the opinion that one can establish the presumption of ownership from the biblical narrative concerning the Shunammite woman (II Kings 8:1–6). Her land was occupied during the time she was fleeing in the Philistine lands, and she required the intercession of the king to recover it.

sections.en: And there are those who say a different version of the previous discussion: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says: One can establish the presumption of ownership with regard to the property of one who is fleeing. Rav Yehuda reports: When I said this ruling before Shmuel, he said to me: Isn’t that obvious? But does the owner actually have to protest in the presence of the possessor?
sections.he: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מַחֲזִיקִים בְּנִכְסֵי בוֹרֵחַ. כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֲמַר לִי: פְּשִׁיטָא! וְכִי לִמְחוֹת בְּפָנָיו הוּא צָרִיךְ?!

en: מְחָאָה f. (מָחָה) protest to prevent the claim of undisturbed possession (see חֲזָקָה). Bava Batra 38ᵃ, and e. מ׳ שלא בפניו הויא מ׳ a protest (before witnesses) in the absence of the usurper is a legal protest (prevents the claim of undisturbed possession being recognized). Ib.ᵇ היכי דמי מ׳ וכ׳ what is a legal protest? If he merely says, This man is a robber, it is not a legal protest. Ib. 39ᵇ, sq. מ׳ בפני שנים ואין וכ׳ a protest is valid, if made in the presence of two witnesses, nor is it necessary to say, Write; i.e. they may write a document to that effect without being especially authorized; and from

en:
מחי, מָחָה, (מָחַח) (Biblical Hebrew; see מָהָה) to rub, wipe out; to wear out, destroy. [In Talmud mostly מָחַק.] Eruvin 13ᵃ; Sotah II, 4 (17ᵇ) (reference. to ומחה, Bamidbar V, 23) כתב שיכול לִמְחוֹת (Mishnah להִמָּחֵק) a writing which one can wash off. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 23 (play on מחויאל, Breishit IV, 18) מוֹחָן אני וכ׳ I shall wipe them out of the world; and e.—V. מָחוּי.

Piël - מִיחָה [to strike out, annul,]
1) to protest against. Bava Batra 38ᵇ מי׳ בפני שנים if he entered a protest against the illegitimate occupation of his property in the presence of two (see מְחָאָה). Ib. וכי למָחוֹת וכ׳ must he protest in the occupant’s presence?—Ketubot 11ᵃ מִיחֲתָה she protested against her conversion in childhood. Pesachim 88ᵃ יכולה למחות she has the privilege of protesting (declaring her preference); and from

—2) (with ב or ביד of the person) to forewarn, interfere, try to prevent. Shabbat 55ᵇ bottom of page מפני שהיה לו … בחפני ולא מי׳ (not לחפני, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) it was for Ph. to forewarn Hofni, and he did not. Ib.ᵃ שאם מִיחוּ בהם לא יקבלו מהם (Manuscript Munich מחו … קבלו) that if they warned them, they would not have heeded them. Pesachim IV, 8, and e. לא מיחו בידם they did not prohibit their doing so; and from—Shir HaShirim Rabbah to IV, 12 עמדו הבנות (ו)מִיחוּ על עצמן וכ׳ the daughters (in their father’s absence) entered a protest concerning themselves and gave themselves away to husbands (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Beshalach, p. 82ᵃ, and e. נתעסקו בעצמן).

Hifil - הִמְחָה
1) to dissolve, dilute. Yerushalmi Pesachim III, beginning 29ᵈ ה׳ את החמץ if (by boiling) he made a mush of the leavened matter (made it unrecognizable). Chullin 120ᵃ; Yerushalmi Ma'aser Sheni II, beginning 53ᵇ, and e., see גָּמָא; and from (interchanging with הִמְהָה).—Tosefta Parah IX (VIII), 8 הִמְחָן באור (not באויר) if he thawed the frozen water by artificial heat.—[Midrash Till. to Psalms VI, 7 וממחה, read וממסה, see מָסָה.]

—2) to rub off, cleanse, polish. Bava Batra V, 10 מַמְחֶה משקלותיו cleanses his weights. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 7 (play on מיחים, Psalms LXVI, 15) כזה שהוא ממחה בקערה like him who wipes a dish (licks the remnants up); Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Eth Korb., p. 61ᵃ; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 16; and e.—Pirké d’R. El. Chaldaic XVII מַמְחָה בכפיה she produces a sound by rubbing her hands (in sympathy with the mourners).

—3) (denominative of מוּמְחֶה) to recognize as an authority; in gen. to authorize; to appoint. Sanhedrin 23ᵃ לא כל הימנו … שהִמְחוּהוּ רבים עליהם he cannot reject a judge whom the majority has recognized as an authority over them. Bava Metzia IX, 12 הִמְחֵהוּ אצל וכ׳ if he gave him an order to the storekeeper. Yerushalmi Pesachim VIII, 35ᵈ top אם במַמְחִין סתם האשה מַמְחָה וכ׳ if by מדעתו is meant giving authority (and not merely knowing and tolerating), it is tacitly understood that a woman makes an appointment as if saying, I will dine with my children; if it means merely knowing, then the Mishnah (Pesachim VIII, 1) means appointment.—[Y. Shabbat XIII, beginning 14ᵃ הממחה צדדיו ed. Krot., see מָתַח.]

Nifal - נִמְחֶה to be dissolved, washed away; to be wiped out, destroyed. Yerushalmi Pesachim III, beginning 29ᵈ a cake boiled שלא נ׳ without being mashed beyond recognition (see supra). Taanit III, 8, and e. אם נִמְחֵית וכ׳, whether the stone … has been washed away, see אֶבֶן. Tosefta Parah l. common gender. נִימּוֹחוּ (from מָחַח) the water was thawed up. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 28. אפי׳ אסטרובולין … נ׳ even the millstone was washed away. Ib. וכמה נימוחו מהם and how many of them were destroyed?; and e.

comments.en:
Therefore, if Shimon lodged a protest in the presence of witnesses, but told them: "Do not utter a word about this protest," the protest is of no consequence. If, however, the witnesses said on their own volition: "We will not utter a word about this," the protest is significant. For a person will ultimately speak of a matter that he was not charged to keep private.
Similarly, if the original owner told the witnesses: "Don't tell the person who took possession of the property about my protest," or the witnesses said on their own volition: "We will not notify him," the protest is of consequence. For even though they will not notify him, they will notify others, and ultimately the information will reach him.

comments.he:
קא משמע לן דאפילו מיחה בפני בני אדם שאינן יכולין לומר לו הויא מחאה. יש לפרש דהכי קאמר, שאפילו ברוח מחמת מרדין, שהוא מתירא מלמחות בפני בני אדם שיכולין להגיד לו, כדי שלא ידע גואל הדם וירדוף אחריו, ואינו מוחה אלא בפני בני אדם זקנים וכיוצא בזה כגון שאינן מכירין אותו שהן בעצמן אינן יכולים להגיד לו, אף על גב דאמרינן חברך חברא אית ליה, אפילו הכי אינו נמנע מלמחות בפני אלו, שהאחרים שיגידו להם אלו שמחיה בפניהם אינן יודעין היכא הוא וגם גואל הדם אינו קם אחריו לרדוף מן הספק, ולפיכך מוחה בפניהן על אלו ומחאתו מחאה.
ושמואל סבר דכל שהוא מוחה בפני בני אדם שהן בעצמן אינן יכולין להגיד לו אינה מחאה. ולפי פירוש זה לית הילכתא כרב אלא כשמואל, חדא דהילכתא כשמואל בדיני, ועוד דקם ליה רבא כותיה, דקאמר הלכתא אין מחזיקין בנכסי בורח ומחאה שלא בפניו הואי מחאה, ואוקימנא כאן בבורח מחמת ממון כאן בבורח מחמת מרדין, אלא דקשיא להדין פירושא, דאם כן מאי קשיא להו, אדרבא דאמר אין מחזיקין בנכסי בירה ומחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה, ואוקימנא כאן בבורח מחמת ממון כאן בבורח מחמת מרדין. אלא דקשיא להדין פירושא, דאם כן מאי קשיא להו, אדרבא דאמר אין מחזיקין בנכסי בורח ומחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה, דאקשינן עליה לתרתי, הא שמואל נמי הרי אמר וכי היכי דניחא להו ההיא דשמואל תינח להו הא דרבא. וי"ל דבורח סתם אפילו ברוח מחמת טימון משמע, והיכינו דקשיא להו עליה דרבא ומשמע דלפיכך אין מחזיקין בנכסי בורח משום דמחאה שלא בפניו לא הויא מחאה, והדר אמר מחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה, ולפיכך הקשו עליו טפי מדשמואל. ואינו מחוור.

If Shimon issued a protest in a distant country, why can Reuven not claim: "I did not hear that he lodged a protest against me so that I felt it necessary to safeguard my deed of acquisition"?
Because we tell him: "Your friend has a friend, and his friend has a friend. And it is an established presumption that word of the protest reached you. Hence, since you know that he lodged a protest against you within the three years, if it is true that you had a deed of acquisition and you did not safeguard it, you caused yourself a loss."

comments.en: The Ri Migash explains that this is not derived from the explicit statement of Rav per se. Rather, it is derived from the fact that Rav made a seemingly unnecessary halakhic statement, presumably intending to add that a protest does not need to be lodged in the presence of witnesses who will report it directly to the possessor. The Ritva explains that it can be inferred from Rav’s statement, as one who is fleeing would not protest before witnesses who would themselves immediately report the protest, as doing so may lead to his whereabouts being discovered. Instead, he would lodge a protest before those who would not be able to report the protest themselves, relying on the fact that word would eventually reach the possessor.
comments.he: ר"י מיגאש מסביר שאין דבר זה נלמד ממשמעות דברי רב, שהרי לא דיבר בענין זה. אלא כיון שהוסיף ואמר הלכה יתירה שלכאורה אינה צריכה, יש ללמוד מכאן שרצה להוסיף שאין המחאה צריכה להיות בפני אנשים שיאמרו לו בעצמם. ועוד הוסיף שאפשר לדייק דבר זה מדברי רב עצמו, שלא הסתפק בנוסח "מחאה שלא בפניו", שניתן לצמצמו למקרה שהשנים עצמם יודיעו למחזיק. וראה בריטב"א המסביר כי הואיל ומדובר בבורח, מן הסתם לא יעשה זאת בפני אנשים המפרסמים את הדבר מיד, שעל ידי כך יתפרסם שהוא בורח, אלא מוחה בפני אלה שאינם יכולים להודיע בעצמם.

comments.en: Protesting in the presence of two witnesses is effective even if they themselves are unable to approach the possessor and inform him of the protest. The reason for this is that the protest will reach the possessor by word of mouth, and this is sufficient to nullify the presumptive ownership (see also the Beit Yosef, citing the Rosh). This is in accordance with the opinion of Rav (Shulĥan Arukh, Ĥoshen Mishpat 146:1).

comments.en: Many commentaries hold that one should not understand from the words of the Gemara that witnesses are needed for the protest to take effect. The witnesses are needed to establish that the protest took place, but if the possessor concedes that it took place, or even if the claimant lodged the protest before two witnesses separately, it is still a valid protest. The same is true of the cases discussed on 40a, those of preemptive declaration, admission, and acquisition. The reason that he states that a protest can be lodged in the presence of two is only to teach that there is no need for three, as opposed to the case of the ratification of documents, as will be discussed (see Rabbeinu Yona). Others question whether lodging a protest in the presence of one witness is effective, as in such a case the possessor could claim that he did not take the protest seriously, since he could have denied its occurrence (Ramban). By contrast, the Ra’avad holds that in all of these cases the witnesses are an integral feature of the protest, and the protest does not take effect if it did not take place in the presence of two witnesses.
comments.sourceHeRef: בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם

sections.en: The Gemara asks: And Rav, who ruled that one can establish the presumption of ownership with regard to the property of one who is fleeing, what is he teaching us, that a protest that is lodged not in his presence is a valid protest? But Rav already said this halakha one time, and he would not need to repeat it. Rather, Rav teaches us this: That even if the owner protested in the presence of two witnesses who are personally unable to tell the possessor about the protest, it is nevertheless a valid protest.
sections.he: וְרַב – מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? מֶחָאָה שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו הָוְיָא מֶחָאָה?! וְהָא אַמְרַהּ רַב חֲדָא זִימְנָא! אֶלָּא הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן – דַּאֲפִילּוּ מִיחָה בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לוֹמַר לוֹ, הָוְיָא מֶחָאָה –

Bava Batra 38ᵃ, and e. מ׳ שלא בפניו הויא מ׳ a protest (before witnesses) in the absence of the usurper is a legal protest (prevents the claim of undisturbed possession being recognized). Ib.ᵇ היכי דמי מ׳ וכ׳ what is a legal protest? If he merely says, This man is a robber, it is not a legal protest. Ib. 39ᵇ, sq. מ׳ בפני שנים ואין וכ׳ a protest is valid, if made in the presence of two witnesses, nor is it necessary to say, Write; i.e. they may write a document to that effect without being especially authorized; and from

comments.en:
Therefore, if Shimon lodged a protest in the presence of witnesses, but told them: "Do not utter a word about this protest," the protest is of no consequence. If, however, the witnesses said on their own volition: "We will not utter a word about this," the protest is significant. For a person will ultimately speak of a matter that he was not charged to keep private.
Similarly, if the original owner told the witnesses: "Don't tell the person who took possession of the property about my protest," or the witnesses said on their own volition: "We will not notify him," the protest is of consequence. For even though they will not notify him, they will notify others, and ultimately the information will reach him.

comments.en:
If Shimon issued a protest in a distant country, why can Reuven not claim: "I did not hear that he lodged a protest against me so that I felt it necessary to safeguard my deed of acquisition"?
Because we tell him: "Your friend has a friend, and his friend has a friend. And it is an established presumption that word of the protest reached you. Hence, since you know that he lodged a protest against you within the three years, if it is true that you had a deed of acquisition and you did not safeguard it, you caused yourself a loss."

sections.en: The Gemara explains: As Rav Anan said: This was explained to me personally by Shmuel himself: If the owner protested in the presence of two people who are able to personally tell the possessor, it is a valid protest, but if the owner protested in the presence of two people who are unable to personally tell the possessor, it is not a valid protest. And why does Rav hold that it is a valid protest? Because your friend who heard the protest has a friend to whom he tells about the protest, and your friend’s friend has a friend to whom he tells about the protest, and so forth. Therefore, word of the protest will reach the possessor.
sections.he: דְּאָמַר רַב עָנָן: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל: מִיחָה בִּפְנֵי שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁיְּכוֹלִים לוֹמַר לוֹ – הָוְיָא מֶחָאָה, מִיחָה בִּפְנֵי שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לוֹמַר לוֹ – לָא הָוְיָא מֶחָאָה. וְרַב – חַבְרָךְ חַבְרָא אִית לֵיהּ, וְחַבְרָא דְחַבְרָךְ חַבְרָא אִית לֵיהּ.

en: *מִרְדִּין m. plural (see מֵרְדָא) rebellious acts, political crimes, especially the unauthorized exercise of criminal jurisdiction by Jews under the Parthian government. Bava Kamma 117ᵃ עד האידנא מלכותא דיוונאי הוו … השתא פרסאי נינהו … ואמרי מ׳ מ׳ Manuscript Munich (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) formerly the rulers were Greeks who cared not about bloodshed (execution by unauthorized courts), but now they are Persians (Parthians) who do care &c., and cry, rebellion! rebellion!—Bava Metzia 39ᵃ בורח מחמת מ׳ who flees from persecution for political offenses; Bava Batra 38ᵇ. [Hai Gaon derives our word from the Persian, giving it the meaning of murder; Fleisher, appendix to Levy’s Targumic or Talmudic Lexicon. to Levy Talmud Dict. III, p. 317ᵇ suggests murdan, to die.]

comments.en: When a person has to flee because of a danger to his life - e.g., the king desired to kill him - a claim of ownership cannot be established with regard to his property. Even if the person in possession of it derived benefit for several years and claimed that he purchased it, the fact that he derived benefit is not significant. We do not tell the owner of the field: "Why didn't you protest?" For the answer is obvious; he was concerned over his life. If, however, a person flees because of financial matters, he is considered like any other person. Thus, if he does not protest, a claim of ownership can be established over his property.

comments.en: One cannot establish presumptive ownership with regard to the property of one who is fleeing for his life, as he is unable to lodge a protest out of fear of revealing his location. If the owner is fleeing merely due to financial difficulties, one is able to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to his property (Rambam Sefer Mishpatim, Hilkhot To’en VeNitan 14:10; Shulĥan Arukh, Ĥoshen Mishpat 143:3).
comments.he: ביטוי זה יש לו שני מובנים, מובן אחד: מדוע אומר החכם שני דברים כשהיה יכול לאומרם רק פעם אחת. ומשמעות אחרת (שהיא המובן המשמש כאן): כיצד אומר החכם שני דברים שמבחינת תוכנם סותרים זה את זה.

comments.en: The Rashbam and others explain that this term refers to killing. Even if he killed another unwittingly, the owner is afraid of being discovered by his victim’s blood redeemer. The Rashba explains that the blood redeemer would pursue the killer to any place he might possibly be found, while a creditor would not go to such lengths. Others understand the term to refer to one who committed treason (Rabbeinu Gershom Meor HaGola). The Rashbam understands that the reason for his not protesting is his fear of being discovered. It would seem that the Rambam understands that he is too preoccupied with his survival to protest about mere monetary matters.

sections.en: Rava says: The halakha is that one cannot establish the presumption of ownership with regard to the property of one who is fleeing, and a protest that is lodged not in a possessor’s presence is a valid protest. The Gemara asks: How can he say these two statements that contradict each other? The Gemara answers: This is not difficult. Here, the second statement, is referring to a case where he is fleeing due to monetary difficulties. In such a case, he is able to ensure that the protest reaches the possessor, while there, the first statement, is referring to a case where he is fleeing due to a charge of killing [meradin]. In such a case, he is unable to publicize his protest out of fear of revealing his whereabouts.

en: מְחָאָה f. (מָחָה) protest to prevent the claim of undisturbed possession (see חֲזָקָה). Bava Batra 38ᵃ, and e. מ׳ שלא בפניו הויא מ׳ a protest (before witnesses) in the absence of the usurper is a legal protest (prevents the claim of undisturbed possession being recognized). Ib.ᵇ היכי דמי מ׳ וכ׳ what is a legal protest? If he merely says, This man is a robber, it is not a legal protest. comments.en:
What constitutes a protest? That the owner says in the presence of two witnesses: "So-and-so who is using my field is a robber. In the future, I will call him to court." Similarly, if he says: "The property is rented out to him or it was given to him as security for a loan. If he claims that I sold it to him or gave it to him as a present, I will lodge a claim against him in court." Similarly, if he makes other analogous statements, the protest is of consequence even though he did not issue it in the country where the person in possession of the land is located.
If, however, he told them merely: "So-and-so who is using my field is a robber," that is not a valid protest, for Reuven will say: "When I heard this, I said to myself: 'Maybe he was merely slandering me.' Therefore, I was not careful about keeping my deed of acquisition."

comments.en: Merely saying: So-and-so is a robber, is not a valid protest. It is necessary to say: So-and-so, who is in possession of my property, is a robber and I intend to bring him to court. The Rema, citing the Rosh and others, writes that it is not necessary to say: And I intend to bring him to court (Rambam Sefer Mishpatim, Hilkhot To’en VeNitan 11:7; Shulĥan Arukh, Ĥoshen Mishpat 146:4).
comments.he: אין זו מחאה, שהרי אין המחזיק יודע מה בדיוק רוצה המערער, ופעמים שאינו חושב שהוא מערער על החזקה בקרקע (רשב"ם). והוסיף רבינו יונה, שאף אם השמיט חלק זה של הדברים, אם אמר "נקיט לה לארעאי בגזלנותא" וכו' — די בכך אבל ריטב"א כתב שאף פרט זה חשוב, שאם אינו מפרש דבר זה יכול המחזיק לחשוב שהלה טוען שלא שילם לו את כל המגיע לו, ולכן צריך לפרש שהוא מאשימו בגזל קרקעו.

sections.en: The Gemara presents a series of disputes with regard to what is considered a valid protest. What manner of statement constitutes a protest? Rav Zevid said: If the owner says in general terms: So-and-so is a robber, it is not a valid protest, but if he says: So-and-so is a robber as he is holding my land through robbery,
